userStories.title: Knowledge state, chunk store, allowlist and configuration
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Establish opt-in repository knowledge configuration, durable repository/file state, a shared-table chunk store, project-scoped service access and fixed corpus selection.

**Motivation** — The existing KB cannot serve this today.

**Approach** — 1c-c-D1 (configuration): `IFleetConfig` (`apps/api/src/config/fleet.config.ts:8-63`) gains `knowledgeIndexEnabled: boolean` and `knowledgePollMs: number`. `FleetConfigSchema` gains `@IsOptional() @IsString() KNOWLEDGE_INDEX_ENABLED: string;` and `@IsOptional() @IsString() KNOWLEDGE_POLL_MS: string;` next to `FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED` (`:96`). The factory sets `knowledgeIndexEnabled: process.env['KNOWLEDGE_INDEX_ENABLED'] === 'true'` (the `threadsEnabled` rule, `:144`) and `knowledgePollMs` = `int('KNOWLEDGE_POLL_MS', 1_800_000)` (`int` at `:99`), replaced by `1_800_000` when it is not a finite number and raised to `60_000` when lower. Milliseconds match `FLEET_PR_REFRESH_MS`.

1c-c-D2 (module): a new `KnowledgeModule` (`apps/api/src/fleet/knowledge/knowledge.module.ts`) imports `RagModule` and `GitBrokerModule`, provides the state repository, `KnowledgeIndexService`, `KnowledgeChunkStore`, `KnowledgeSearchService`, `KnowledgeRepoIndexer`, `KnowledgeIndexQueue`, `KnowledgePoller` and `ProjectKnowledgeController`, and exports `KnowledgeIndexService`, `KnowledgeSearchService` and `KnowledgeIndexQueue` only. `KnowledgeIndexService` is the service face over the state repository (the api-data layering rule: controllers and other modules never inject the repository): `resolveProjectRepo(projectId, ref: { repoId: string } | { owner: string; name: string }): Promise<KnowledgeRepoRef | null>` answers the repository only when it is one of `findProjectRepos(projectId)`, `listProjectRepos(projectId)` returns those repositories, and `listProjectStates(projectId)` returns them joined with their `KnowledgeRepoIndex` rows. `KnowledgeRepoRef` is `{ id, projectId, provider, owner, name, defaultBranch, githubInstallationId }`. `FleetModule` (`apps/api/src/fleet/fleet.module.ts`), `AssistantModule` (`apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/assistant.module.ts`) and `FleetTicketsModule` (`apps/api/src/fleet/tickets/fleet-tickets.module.ts`) import it. `RagModule`'s `exports` (`apps/api/src/rag/rag.module.ts:114`) gains `EmbeddingService`. No cycle: `RagModule` and `GitBrokerModule` import no fleet module.
Staging: US-001 creates KnowledgeModule with state repository, KnowledgeIndexService and KnowledgeChunkStore and exports only the service available now; US-002, US-004 and US-005 add their providers/exports when implemented. FleetModule imports it now; AssistantModule and FleetTicketsModule imports accompany their consumers in US-006 and US-005. Do not introduce unresolved future providers.

1c-c-D3 (state tables): migration `20261020090000_knowledge_index` adds the models in Interface, and `FleetRepo` gains the back-relations `knowledgeIndex KnowledgeRepoIndex?` and `knowledgeFiles KnowledgeRepoFile[]`. `PrismaKnowledgeIndexRepository` (behind `KNOWLEDGE_INDEX_REPOSITORY`, module-private) owns both tables and the read of indexable repositories: `findRepo(repoId)`, `findProjectRepos(projectId)` (ordered `createdAt`, then `id`, at most 60, as `PrismaFleetJobRepository.findProjectRepos`), `findAllGithubRepos()` (every GitHub repository with a non-null `githubInstallationId`, at most 500), `claim(repoId, projectId, now, leaseMs)`, `renew(repoId, leaseUntil): Promise<boolean>`, `finish(repoId, result)`, `listFiles(repoId)`, `upsertFile`, `deleteFile`, `listStates(projectId)`.

1c-c-D4 (chunk rows): a repository chunk is one `LanceRecord` (`apps/api/src/rag/lance-table-manager.ts:18-30`) in table `project_<projectId>`: `id = repo:<repoId>:<path>#<chunkIndex>`, `source = 'repo'`, `source_id = repo:<repoId>:<path>`, `content` = the context line, a newline, the abstract, a blank line, then the chunk text (so full-text search also matches the context line), `vector` = the embedding of `content`, `metadata` = `JSON.stringify` of `{ repoId, owner, name, path, sha, blobSha, title, headingPath, anchor, chunkIndex, chunkCount, abstract, text, status?, supersededBy? }`, `created_at` = the pass time, and `provider` / `model` = the embedding provider and model, or `provider: 'none'` and `model: ''` with a zero vector of the table's dimension when the embedding failed (1c-c-D6). The context line is `<owner>/<name> · <path> · <headingPath>`, with `headingPath` the H1-H3 titles joined by ` > `; for chunk 0, whose `headingPath` is empty, it is `<owner>/<name> · <path>`.

1c-c-D5 (chunk store): `KnowledgeChunkStore` wraps `LanceTableManager` (`lance-table-manager.ts:130`). Every write runs inside `exclusive('project_' + projectId, fn)` (`:369`) on the table from `getOrCreateTable` (`:231`): `replaceFile(projectId, sourceId, rows)` deletes `source_id = '<sourceId>'` then adds all rows in one `add` call; `deleteFile(projectId, sourceId)` deletes them. It never calls `addRecord` (`:395`), whose per-row delete-by-`source_id` would drop a file's other chunks. `readFile(projectId, sourceId)` returns the file's rows (at most 2000) parsed into `KnowledgeChunkRow` = `{ id, sourceId, provider }` plus every `metadata` field of 1c-c-D4, sorted by `chunkIndex`; `lexical` and `vector` return the same parsed shape. Every `sourceId` a method receives must pass `isSafeFilterValue` (`lance-table-manager.ts:37`), else the method throws `KnowledgeInvalidPathError`. `lexical(projectId, query, predicate, limit)` runs `table.query().fullTextSearch(query, { columns: 'content' }).where(predicate).limit(limit)` and `vector(projectId, embedding, predicate, limit)` runs `table.vectorSearch(embedding).distanceType('cosine').where(predicate).limit(limit)` (LanceDB 0.17 `QueryBase.where`). When `LanceTableManager.available` is false (in-memory mode), every method throws `KnowledgeStoreUnavailableError`. After a pass that wrote or deleted rows, the indexer calls `RagService.optimizeTable(projectId)` (`apps/api/src/rag/rag.service.ts:134`) once, so the full-text index covers the new rows. US-004 owns that indexer call.

Allowlist contract from 1c-c-D9 step 7: The allowlist (pure `isIndexablePath(path: string): boolean` and `selectIndexableEntries(entries: ForgeTreeEntry[]): { kept: ForgeTreeEntry[]; skipped: number; capMessage: string | null }` in `apps/api/src/fleet/knowledge/knowledge-allowlist.ts`) keeps blob entries whose path is `README.md`, `.nax/context.md`, `AGENTS.md` (only when `.nax/context.md` is not in the tree), matches `docs/**/*.md`, or matches `.nax/features/<one segment>/spec.md`. It skips (and counts in `skippedCount`) an entry over 262144 bytes, an entry whose path fails `isSafeFilterValue` (`lance-table-manager.ts:37`), and every entry after the first 2000 kept (`capMessage` `2000-file cap reached`).

**Scope** — In: schema and SQL migration, config and existing config tests, testFleetConfig defaults `knowledgeIndexEnabled: false` / `knowledgePollMs: 1_800_000` preserving all keys and overrides, repository/service/module, chunk store and allowlist. Add a co-located DB-free KnowledgeModule compilation spec and native LanceDB/Postgres integration fixture. Out: search/controller (US-002), chunking (US-003), indexer/embedding policy (US-004), queue/triggers/routes (US-005), tools (US-006), evaluation (US-007); no configurable paths, ticket retrieval changes or deleted-repo chunk cleanup.

**Interface** — Exact state models:
```prisma
model KnowledgeRepoIndex {
  repoId          String    @id
  projectId       String
  status          String    @default("idle") // idle | running | failed | skipped
  indexedSha      String?
  fileCount       Int       @default(0)
  chunkCount      Int       @default(0)
  unembeddedCount Int       @default(0)
  skippedCount    Int       @default(0)
  lastError       String?
  leaseUntil      DateTime?
  startedAt       DateTime?
  finishedAt      DateTime?
  updatedAt       DateTime  @updatedAt
  repo            FleetRepo @relation(fields: [repoId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  @@index([projectId])
}

model KnowledgeRepoFile {
  repoId          String
  path            String
  blobSha         String
  chunkCount      Int
  unembeddedCount Int       @default(0)
  updatedAt       DateTime  @updatedAt
  repo            FleetRepo @relation(fields: [repoId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  @@id([repoId, path])
}
```
`resolveProjectRepo(projectId, ref: { repoId: string } | { owner: string; name: string }): Promise<KnowledgeRepoRef | null>`; `isIndexablePath(path: string): boolean`; `selectIndexableEntries(entries: ForgeTreeEntry[]): { kept: ForgeTreeEntry[]; skipped: number; capMessage: string | null }`; `renew(repoId, leaseUntil): Promise<boolean>`; chunk-store signatures and KnowledgeChunkRow shape are specified verbatim above.

[unit] fleetConfig() with KNOWLEDGE_INDEX_ENABLED=true and KNOWLEDGE_POLL_MS=5000 resolves knowledgeIndexEnabled: true and knowledgePollMs: 60000.

[unit] Test.createTestingModule({ imports: [KnowledgeModule] }) with PrismaService, TRANSACTION_MANAGER and the RAG_CFG / FLEET_CFG configs provided as stubs compiles, and KnowledgeChunkStore resolves from it.

[integration] PrismaKnowledgeIndexRepository.claim(repoId, projectId, now, 900000) on a repository with no state row creates it with status: 'running' and leaseUntil = now + 15 minutes and answers true, and a second claim at now + 1 minute answers false.
[integration] After a claim at now, a claim at now + 16 minutes answers true.
[integration] Deleting a FleetRepo row deletes its KnowledgeRepoIndex and KnowledgeRepoFile rows.

[integration] On a real LanceDB in a mkdtempSync directory, KnowledgeChunkStore.replaceFile(p, 'repo:r1:docs/a.md', [row0, row1, row2]) followed by readFile(p, 'repo:r1:docs/a.md') returns the three rows in chunkIndex order.

[unit] selectIndexableEntries keeps AGENTS.md when the entries hold no .nax/context.md, and drops it when they do.

userStories.title: Hybrid search service and search route
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add project-isolated RRF repository-doc retrieval and a member search endpoint without changing existing ticket search.

**Motivation** — Its search has no source filter, so repository chunks added to it would crowd ticket results.

**Approach** — 1c-c-R6 (isolation): repository chunks share the project's LanceDB table but a separate search path; ticket search and its weighted fusion are unchanged.

1c-c-D7 (search): `KnowledgeSearchService` depends on `KnowledgeChunkStore`, `EmbeddingService` and `KnowledgeIndexService`. `readDoc(projectId, repoId, path): Promise<KnowledgeChunkRow[]>` returns `KnowledgeChunkStore.readFile(projectId, 'repo:' + repoId + ':' + path)`; it is the only read path `koda_get_doc` uses. `search({ projectId, query, repoId?, pathPrefix?, limit })` returns `{ lexicalOnly: boolean; empty: boolean; hits: KnowledgeHit[] }`, where `KnowledgeHit` is `{ repoId, owner, name, path, sha, anchor, headingPath, title, abstract, snippet, status?, supersededBy?, score }` and `snippet` is the first 400 characters of the chunk text. The base predicate is `source = 'repo'`, plus `AND source_id LIKE 'repo:<repoId>:%'` when `repoId` is given. The lexical leg asks 50 rows (200 when `pathPrefix` is given, because the prefix is applied after the legs). AC-authoritative vector predicate construction: start `source = 'repo' AND provider != 'none'`, then append `AND source_id LIKE 'repo:<repoId>:%'` when restricted, so both predicates end with the repo clause. The vector leg embeds the query with `EmbeddingService.embed` and asks the same number of rows. When the query embedding throws, the vector leg is skipped and `lexicalOnly` is true. The legs fuse by reciprocal rank fusion, `score(row) = Σ 1 / (60 + rank)` over the legs the row appears in (rank 1-based), ties broken by row `id` ascending. Hits whose `repoId` is not among `KnowledgeIndexService.listProjectRepos(projectId)` are dropped (a deleted fleet repository's chunks), then hits whose `path` does not start with `pathPrefix` are dropped, then the list is cut to `limit`. `empty` is true when the project's table holds no `repo` row at all.

1c-c-D12 (routes, search portion): `ProjectKnowledgeController` at `projects/:slug/knowledge`, `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard)` with `@ApiParam({ name: 'slug' })` (the `ProjectFleetReposController` pattern) and `@CurrentProject()`:
- `POST search` (member, HTTP 200): body `{ query: string (1-500), repo?: "owner/name", pathPrefix?: string (1-300, no `..`, no leading `/`), limit?: integer 1-50 (default 20) }`; any other body answers 400, answers `{ lexicalOnly, empty, hits }` from `KnowledgeSearchService`; an unknown `repo` answers 404 `knowledge.repoNotFound`.
- `POST reindex` and `POST search` answer 409 `knowledge.disabled` when `knowledgeIndexEnabled` is false (`ConflictAppException`, the `threads.disabled` pattern, `apps/api/src/fleet/threads/threads.service.ts:30`). The i18n keys go to `apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}/knowledge.json`. Reindex is implemented by US-005, not here.
Search route on an unavailable store: 409 `knowledge.unavailable`. i18n files contain nested `disabled.409`, `unavailable.409`, `repoNotFound.404` keys, as threads.json nests disabled.409. Resolve `repo` through KnowledgeIndexService.resolveProjectRepo within the caller's project, never through repository injection in the controller. Preserve JsonResponse envelopes.

Add KnowledgeSearchService and ProjectKnowledgeController to the US-001 KnowledgeModule and export KnowledgeSearchService. Route cases go into `apps/api/test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts` with KnowledgeSearchService stubbed. Extend the upstream `knowledge-store.integration.spec.ts` for real native LanceDB search with fake embeddings and both embedded/unembedded rows. Regenerate `openapi.json` with `bun run api:export-spec` and the CLI client with `bun run generate` from repo root; generated types.gen.ts/sdk.gen.ts are never hand-edited.

**Scope** — In: search/readDoc service, search request/result DTOs and route, membership/repo/path input checks, translations and generated contract. Out: state/reindex routes and queue/poller (US-005), indexer (US-004), agent presentation (US-006), evaluation caller (US-007); no ticket fusion edits, cross-project search, reranker/Jina or deletion of stale repository chunks.

**Interface** — `readDoc(projectId, repoId, path): Promise<KnowledgeChunkRow[]>`; `search({ projectId, query, repoId?, pathPrefix?, limit })`; return `{ lexicalOnly: boolean; empty: boolean; hits: KnowledgeHit[] }`; `KnowledgeHit` is `{ repoId, owner, name, path, sha, anchor, headingPath, title, abstract, snippet, status?, supersededBy?, score }`. Controller exports `KnowledgeSearchBodyDto` and `KnowledgeSearchResultDto`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] KnowledgeSearchService.search with a stub store whose lexical leg returns rows [a, b] and vector leg returns [b, c] returns hits in the order b, a, c, with b's score equal to 1/61 + 1/62.
[unit] search passes the lexical leg the predicate source = 'repo' and the vector leg source = 'repo' AND provider != 'none'.
[unit] With repoId: 'r1', both predicates end with AND source_id LIKE 'repo:r1:%'.
[unit] When EmbeddingService.embed throws, search never calls the vector leg, returns the lexical hits and lexicalOnly: true.
[unit] A hit whose repoId is not returned by the stubbed KnowledgeIndexService.listProjectRepos(projectId) is absent from the result.
[unit] With pathPrefix: 'docs/adr/', both legs are asked for 200 rows, only hits whose path starts with docs/adr/ are returned, and the result is cut to limit after that filter.
[unit] search on a project whose table holds no source = 'repo' row returns a result with empty: true and hits: [], alongside the result's lexicalOnly boolean.

[integration] On a real LanceDB holding one embedded and one provider: 'none' chunk of the same text, search with the fake embedding provider returns both hits, and the provider: 'none' hit's score is 1/(60 + its lexical rank).

[integration] POST /api/projects/:slug/knowledge/search as a project member with { query: 'broker', repo: 'o/n', limit: 5 } calls KnowledgeSearchService.search with the project's id, the repoId of o/n and limit: 5, and answers 200 with its { lexicalOnly, empty, hits }.
[integration] POST /api/projects/:slug/knowledge/search with an empty query, and with pathPrefix: '../x', answers 400 (one table-driven test).
[integration] POST /api/projects/:slug/knowledge/search with repo: 'o/missing' answers 404.
[integration] POST /api/projects/:slug/knowledge/search with knowledgeIndexEnabled: false answers 409.
[integration] When KnowledgeSearchService.search throws KnowledgeStoreUnavailableError, POST /api/projects/:slug/knowledge/search answers 409.
[integration] POST /api/projects/:slug/knowledge/search by a user who is not a project member answers 403.

routing.reasoning: RRF and native store integration span a new service, guarded HTTP contract and generated client; project membership and repository isolation require strict security TDD.

KnowledgeSearchService.search orders equal RRF scores by row id ascending.
POST /api/projects/:slug/knowledge/search answers 404 knowledge.repoNotFound when repo names a repository belonging only to another project.
POST /api/projects/:slug/knowledge/search answers 400 when the request contains an unknown property instead of silently stripping it.

userStories.title: Markdown heading chunker
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement deterministic Markdown heading chunks, extractive abstracts, summary text, metadata and citation anchors as a pure helper.

**Motivation** — The 2026-10-15 knowledge research found that koda's gap is content and reach, not retrieval sophistication: the project's architecture, specs, design documents and ADRs live as repository Markdown that no thread can reach.

**Approach** — 1c-c-D8 (chunker): `chunkMarkdown(input: { path: string; text: string }): MarkdownChunk[]` in `apps/api/src/fleet/knowledge/markdown-chunker.ts` is pure. `MarkdownChunk` is `{ chunkIndex, title, headingPath, anchor, abstract, text, status?, supersededBy? }`. Rules, in order (the indexer decodes `ForgeFile.content` as UTF-8, invalid bytes becoming U+FFFD, and the chunker first normalises `
` to `
`; an empty text yields chunk 0 only, holding the title; a front matter block with no closing `---` line is ordinary text):
1. A leading YAML front matter block (`---` line, lines, `---` line) is removed from the text; its `title`, `status`, `description` and `superseded-by` keys are read as plain `key: value` strings.
2. The title is the front matter `title`, else the first H1 text, else the file name without `.md`.
3. Sections start at ATX headings of level 1 to 3 (`#`, `##`, `###` followed by a space; trailing `#` characters and spaces are removed from the heading text) outside fenced code blocks (a fence opens and closes on a line starting with three backticks or three tildes). Text before the first heading is a section whose heading path is the title.
4. A section of fewer than 200 characters merges into the following section (its text first), and the merged chunk keeps the following section's `headingPath` and `anchor`; a short last section merges into the previous one, which keeps its own `headingPath` and `anchor`.
5. A section of more than 2000 characters splits at blank lines outside fences into parts of at most 2000 characters each; a single paragraph longer than 2000 characters is its own part. Parts keep the section's heading path and anchor.
6. Chunk 0 is the document summary: `headingPath` and `anchor` are empty, `text` is the title, the front matter `description` (else the first paragraph of the first section), and a line `Sections: ` followed by the H2 titles joined by `; `. Section chunks follow from index 1.
7. `abstract` is the first two sentences of the chunk text (a sentence ends at `. `, `? `, `! ` or a line break), after skipping heading lines, fenced blocks and list markers, cut to 300 characters; empty when nothing remains.
8. `anchor` follows GitHub's heading ids restricted to ASCII: lower-case, drop every character that is not `a-z`, `0-9`, space, hyphen or underscore, replace each space with `-`; a repeated anchor in one file gets `-1`, `-2`, ... in order.
9. `status` and `supersededBy` come from the front matter and are copied onto every chunk of the file.

Use ordinary pure TypeScript text helpers, not Nest providers or an LLM. Sanity-check representative real design Markdown but keep unit tests deterministic and independent of its changing prose.

**Scope** — In: new markdown-chunker.ts and its co-located unit spec; ordered extraction/merge/split/summary/anchor rules. Out: GitHub decoding and indexing calls (US-004), store/state/config (US-001), search (US-002), tools/citation parsing (US-006); no Setext section headings, non-ASCII anchor preservation or model-written abstracts.

**Interface** — `chunkMarkdown(input: { path: string; text: string }): MarkdownChunk[]`; `MarkdownChunk` is `{ chunkIndex, title, headingPath, anchor, abstract, text, status?, supersededBy? }`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] chunkMarkdown({ path: 'docs/a.md', text }) for a text with an H1 Alpha, an H2 Beta and an H2 Gamma, each section over 200 characters, returns chunk 0 with empty headingPath and anchor and text containing Sections: Beta; Gamma, then chunks with headingPath Alpha, Alpha > Beta and Alpha > Gamma.
[unit] A ## Not a heading line inside a block fenced with three backticks, or with three tildes, does not start a section (one table-driven test).

[unit] A text starting with a front matter block holding title: Decision 7, status: superseded and superseded-by: docs/adr/0009.md returns chunks whose title is Decision 7 and which all carry status: 'superseded' and supersededBy: 'docs/adr/0009.md'.
[unit] No chunk of that front-matter text includes the front matter lines in its text.
[unit] With no front matter and no H1, the title is the file name without .md (docs/guide-x.md gives guide-x).
[unit] A 150-character section between two long sections merges into the following section, whose chunk text starts with the short section's text and whose anchor is the following section's.
[unit] A trailing section of 150 characters merges into the previous section.
[unit] A 5000-character section made of 500-character paragraphs splits into chunks of at most 2000 characters each, all with the section's headingPath and anchor.
[unit] A single 3000-character paragraph is one chunk of 3000 characters.
[unit] The heading ## Token Broker: cache & reuse gets the anchor token-broker-cache--reuse.
[unit] Two headings ## Notes in one file get the anchors notes and notes-1.
[unit] A 400-character H2 section whose body starts 'First sentence. Second one! Third.' gets the abstract 'First sentence. Second one!'.
[unit] A 400-character H2 section whose body is a fenced block, then the line '- Item one. Done.', then further text, gets the abstract 'Item one. Done.'.
[unit] Text before the first heading becomes chunk 1 with the title as its headingPath, and chunk 0's text holds the front matter description when present.
[unit] A text with \r\n line ends returns the same chunks as the same text with \n, and the heading ## Notes ## gives the heading text Notes and the anchor notes.

routing.reasoning: A pure helper and unit spec with a fully specified deterministic algorithm; nuanced fences/merges/anchors but no external systems, permissions or runtime state.

suggestedCriteria: chunkMarkdown({ path: 'docs/empty.md', text: '' }) returns only chunk 0 holding the title empty.
chunkMarkdown preserves an unclosed leading --- front matter block as ordinary text instead of removing it.
chunkMarkdown never cuts a generated abstract beyond 300 characters.

userStories.title: Repository indexer pass
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Incrementally index each repository's allowlisted default-branch Markdown with leases, chunk embeddings, deletions, retryable fallback and durable pass results.

**Motivation** — Neither lets an agent find "where was the token broker's cache designed and why" across a project's documents: the brief is capped at a few kilobytes, and grepping code finds the implementation, not the rationale.

**Approach** — 1c-c-D9 (indexer pass): `KnowledgeRepoIndexer.indexRepo(repoId, now = new Date()): Promise<IndexPassResult>`, with `IndexPassResult = { status: 'indexed' | 'unchanged' | 'skipped' | 'failed' | 'busy'; reason?: string }`:
1. `findRepo(repoId)`; unknown resolves `{ status: 'failed', reason: 'unknown repo' }` with no state written.
2. A non-GitHub repository, or one with a null `githubInstallationId`, records state `skipped` with `lastError` `not a GitHub repository` / `no installation` and resolves `skipped`.
3. `claim(repoId, projectId, now, 900_000)` atomically sets `status: running`, `startedAt`, and `leaseUntil = now + 15 min` only when the row is absent, not `running`, or `leaseUntil < now`; otherwise it resolves `busy` and nothing else runs.
4. `mintReadOnlyToken(githubInstallationId, name)`, then `getBranchHead(token, owner, name, defaultBranch)` (`apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/github-app-client.ts:69,148`).
5. When the head equals `indexedSha` and no `KnowledgeRepoFile` row of the repository has `unembeddedCount > 0`, the pass finishes `idle` with counts unchanged and resolves `unchanged`.
6. `getTree(token, owner, name, head, true)` (`:159`); a `truncated` tree fails the pass with `tree truncated`.
7. The allowlist (pure `isIndexablePath(path: string): boolean` and `selectIndexableEntries(entries: ForgeTreeEntry[]): { kept: ForgeTreeEntry[]; skipped: number; capMessage: string | null }` in `apps/api/src/fleet/knowledge/knowledge-allowlist.ts`) keeps blob entries whose path is `README.md`, `.nax/context.md`, `AGENTS.md` (only when `.nax/context.md` is not in the tree), matches `docs/**/*.md`, or matches `.nax/features/<one segment>/spec.md`. It skips (and counts in `skippedCount`) an entry over 262144 bytes, an entry whose path fails `isSafeFilterValue` (`lance-table-manager.ts:37`), and every entry after the first 2000 kept (`capMessage` `2000-file cap reached`).
8. A kept file whose `KnowledgeRepoFile.blobSha` equals the tree entry's `sha` and whose `unembeddedCount` is 0 is left alone. Every other kept file is read with `getFile(token, owner, name, path, head)` (`:174`), at most four at a time, chunked, embedded (1c-c-D6) and written with `replaceFile`; its `KnowledgeRepoFile` row is upserted and the lease is renewed with `renew(repoId, new Date(clock() + 900_000))` (`clock` is an injectable dependency defaulting to `Date.now`). `renew` answers false when the row is no longer this pass's lease (another claim took it); the pass then stops at once, writes no further rows or state, and resolves `{ status: 'failed', reason: 'lease lost' }`. An `embedBatch` call that has not settled within 120 seconds counts as a failed embedding (1c-c-D6). A `getFile` answer of null treats the file as removed.
9. Every `KnowledgeRepoFile` row whose path is no longer kept has its chunks removed with `deleteFile` and its row deleted.
10. The pass finishes `idle` with `indexedSha = head`, the file, chunk, unembedded and skipped counts, `lastError` null (or the `capMessage`), `leaseUntil` null and `finishedAt`; when it wrote or deleted rows it then optimizes once (1c-c-D5); it resolves `indexed`.
11. Any thrown error after the claim (a mint, `getBranchHead`, `getTree` or `getFile` failure, or `KnowledgeStoreUnavailableError`) finishes the pass `failed` with `lastError` = `RepoCheckException.reason` or the error message cut to 500 characters, `leaseUntil` null, and resolves `failed`; `indexedSha` is not advanced.

1c-c-D6 (embedding): the indexer embeds each changed file's chunk contents with `EmbeddingService.embedBatch(contents)` (`apps/api/src/rag/embedding.service.ts:42`). When it throws, or returns a vector count or length that differs from the chunk count or `EmbeddingService.dimensions`, every chunk of that file is stored unembedded (1c-c-D4), the file's `unembeddedCount` is its chunk count, and the pass logs one warning. The existing `VectorStore` zero-vector fallback (`vector-store.service.ts:198-206`) is unchanged.

1c-c-D4 (chunk rows): a repository chunk is one `LanceRecord` (`apps/api/src/rag/lance-table-manager.ts:18-30`) in table `project_<projectId>`: `id = repo:<repoId>:<path>#<chunkIndex>`, `source = 'repo'`, `source_id = repo:<repoId>:<path>`, `content` = the context line, a newline, the abstract, a blank line, then the chunk text (so full-text search also matches the context line), `vector` = the embedding of `content`, `metadata` = `JSON.stringify` of `{ repoId, owner, name, path, sha, blobSha, title, headingPath, anchor, chunkIndex, chunkCount, abstract, text, status?, supersededBy? }`, `created_at` = the pass time, and `provider` / `model` = the embedding provider and model, or `provider: 'none'` and `model: ''` with a zero vector of the table's dimension when the embedding failed (1c-c-D6). The context line is `<owner>/<name> · <path> · <headingPath>`, with `headingPath` the H1-H3 titles joined by ` > `; for chunk 0, whose `headingPath` is empty, it is `<owner>/<name> · <path>`.

Every unit case runs KnowledgeRepoIndexer.indexRepo with a fake GitHubAppClient, a stub KnowledgeChunkStore, the fake embedding provider, and a stub state repository whose findRepo('r1') resolves a GitHub repository o/n with installation 5n and claim answers true, unless stated. Decode ForgeFile.content as UTF-8 with invalid bytes becoming U+FFFD and call US-003 chunkMarkdown; call US-001 selectIndexableEntries, KnowledgeChunkStore and module-private state repository rather than alternate implementations. Add KnowledgeRepoIndexer as a private KnowledgeModule provider. Fetch concurrency is at most four, but commit ordering must enforce AC8: on first failed renew, only one replaceFile has occurred and no finish occurs. Never log/persist minted tokens or hold a database transaction across HTTP/embeddings. The injectable clock and fake timers support lease/120-second tests.

**Scope** — In: one repo pass, file chunk/embedding row construction, all state transitions, deletion/retry/lease behavior and optimize-once seam. Out: state/store/allowlist implementations (US-001), chunker algorithm (US-003), queue/poll/merge/admin invocation (US-005), search and agent tools (US-002/US-006); only default branch, no GitLab indexing, no outcomes corpus, no changed ticket fallback, no extra multi-instance coordinator or per-repository chunk cap.

**Interface** — `KnowledgeRepoIndexer.indexRepo(repoId, now = new Date()): Promise<IndexPassResult>`; `IndexPassResult = { status: 'indexed' | 'unchanged' | 'skipped' | 'failed' | 'busy'; reason?: string }`. Existing collaborators: `EmbeddingService.embedBatch(texts): Promise<number[][]>`, `RagService.optimizeTable(projectId): Promise<void>`, `GitHubAppClient.mintReadOnlyToken(installationId: bigint, repoName: string): Promise<{ token; expiresAt }>`, `getBranchHead(token, owner, name, branch): Promise<string>`, `getTree(token, owner, name, treeish, recursive): Promise<{ entries: ForgeTreeEntry[]; truncated: boolean }>`, `getFile(token, owner, name, path, ref): Promise<ForgeFile | null>`.

userStories.title: Index queue, poll, merge hook, reindex and state routes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Keep knowledge fresh through a bounded queue, configurable head poll, successful fleet merge hook and ADMIN reindex endpoint, and expose repository index state to members.

**Motivation** — The 2026-10-15 knowledge research found that koda's gap is content and reach, not retrieval sophistication: the project's architecture, specs, design documents and ADRs live as repository Markdown that no thread can reach.

**Approach** — 1c-c-D10 (queue): `KnowledgeIndexQueue.enqueue(repoId, reason: 'poll' | 'merge' | 'admin')` adds the id to an in-process FIFO unless it is already waiting, and drains one `indexRepo` at a time; it never throws and logs a failed pass with `Logger.warn`. When `knowledgeIndexEnabled` is false, `enqueue` does nothing. The waiting set is capped at 1000 ids (a full queue drops the new id with a warning).

1c-c-D11 (triggers): `KnowledgePoller` (`OnModuleInit`/`OnModuleDestroy`, the `FleetPrStateRefresher` timer pattern, `apps/api/src/fleet/tickets/fleet-pr-state.refresher.ts:49-53`) starts `setInterval(() => void this.poll(), knowledgePollMs)` only when `knowledgeIndexEnabled`; `poll()` enqueues every `findAllGithubRepos()` id with reason `poll`. `FleetPrStateRefresher` gains a constructor dependency `knowledge: KnowledgeIndexQueue`; in `apply` (`:120-128`), when `next === 'merged'` and `applyMergedPr` answers `'updated'`, it calls `knowledge.enqueue(link.repo.id, 'merge')`. A link already `merged` is no longer refreshable (`findRefreshableFleetLinks`, `prisma-fleet-tickets.repository.ts:183-187`), and `apply` returns early when the state is unchanged, so a merge enqueues once.

1c-c-D12 (routes, state/reindex portion): `ProjectKnowledgeController` at `projects/:slug/knowledge`, `@UseGuards(ProjectMembershipGuard)` with `@ApiParam({ name: 'slug' })` (the `ProjectFleetReposController` pattern) and `@CurrentProject()`:
- `GET repos` (member): `{ enabled, repos: KnowledgeRepoStateDto[] }`, one entry per `findProjectRepos` repository: `{ repoId, owner, name, provider, status, indexedSha, fileCount, chunkCount, unembeddedCount, skippedCount, lastError, startedAt, finishedAt }`, `status` `never` when no state row exists. Answers even when disabled.
- `POST repos/:repoId/reindex` (`@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')`, HTTP 202): enqueues `admin` and answers `{ queued: true }`; 404 `knowledge.repoNotFound` when the repository is not one of the project's.
- `POST reindex` and `POST search` answer 409 `knowledge.disabled` when `knowledgeIndexEnabled` is false (`ConflictAppException`, the `threads.disabled` pattern, `apps/api/src/fleet/threads/threads.service.ts:30`). The i18n keys go to `apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}/knowledge.json`. The concrete reindex route is repos/:repoId/reindex above; retain US-002 search behavior.

Complete KnowledgeModule by adding private KnowledgeIndexQueue/KnowledgePoller providers and exporting KnowledgeIndexQueue alongside KnowledgeIndexService/KnowledgeSearchService only. FleetTicketsModule imports KnowledgeModule for the queue. Poller may inject the module-private state repository; controllers and other modules use only KnowledgeIndexService for project state/repo checks. The list uses listProjectStates(projectId), preserving all project fleet repos, including non-GitHub and never-indexed rows. Poller enumerates the module-private repository's findAllGithubRepos, bounded to 500 installed GitHub repos. Clean up/unref the timer using the existing refresher lifecycle pattern. Queue failures include both returned failed IndexPassResult and thrown errors; warn and continue, never reject the enqueue caller.

Update `apps/api/src/fleet/tickets/fleet-pr-state.refresher.spec.ts`'s `new FleetPrStateRefresher(...)` call at :32 with a stub KnowledgeIndexQueue eighth argument; every existing assertion is unchanged. Route cases go into `apps/api/test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts` with KnowledgeIndexQueue stubbed. Regenerate `openapi.json` with `bun run api:export-spec` and CLI client with `bun run generate`, preserving US-002 search output; generated types.gen.ts/sdk.gen.ts are never hand-edited.

**Scope** — In: FIFO/poller, merge-only queue integration, reindex/state DTOs and routes, KnowledgeModule/FleetTicketsModule wiring and contract regeneration. Out: implementing search (US-002), indexing algorithm (US-004), tools (US-006), evaluation (US-007); no push webhook or durable queue, and no web status/reindex UI.

**Interface** — `KnowledgeIndexQueue.enqueue(repoId, reason: 'poll' | 'merge' | 'admin')`; `KnowledgePoller.onModuleInit`, `onModuleDestroy`, `poll()`; `GET /api/projects/:slug/knowledge/repos` returns `{ enabled, repos: KnowledgeRepoStateDto[] }`; `POST /api/projects/:slug/knowledge/repos/:repoId/reindex` returns HTTP 202 `{ queued: true }`; state fields are `{ repoId, owner, name, provider, status, indexedSha, fileCount, chunkCount, unembeddedCount, skippedCount, lastError, startedAt, finishedAt }`.

[unit] While a pass for r0 is still running, enqueuing r1, then r2, then r1 again runs indexRepo for r0, r1 and r2 once each, in that order.
[unit] enqueue with knowledgeIndexEnabled: false never calls indexRepo.
[unit] When indexRepo rejects, enqueue does not throw, Logger.warn is called once, and the next queued id still runs.
[unit] With 1000 ids waiting, enqueue of a new id does not add it and calls Logger.warn.
[unit] KnowledgePoller.onModuleInit with knowledgeIndexEnabled: false starts no timer.
[unit] KnowledgePoller.poll() enqueues every findAllGithubRepos() id with reason poll.

[unit] refresh() with the same link already in state merged calls enqueue zero times.

[integration] POST /api/projects/:slug/knowledge/repos/:repoId/reindex as a global ADMIN answers 202 { queued: true } and calls KnowledgeIndexQueue.enqueue(repoId, 'admin').
[integration] The reindex route as a project DEVELOPER answers 403, and as a global ADMIN for a repository of another project answers 404.
[integration] The reindex route with knowledgeIndexEnabled: false answers 409.

[integration] GET /api/projects/:slug/knowledge/repos as a project member answers 200 with one entry per fleet repository of the project, status: 'never' for a repository with no state row, and enabled equal to knowledgeIndexEnabled.

userStories.title: Agent tools and instructions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let member-authorized thread agents search project documentation and read indexed documents/sections through two fenced, citation-producing tools. **Motivation** — Neither lets an agent find "where was the token broker's cache designed and why" across a project's documents: the brief is capped at a few kilobytes, and grepping code finds the implementation, not the rationale. **Approach** — 1c-c-D13 (tools): the tool factories `kbSearchTool(deps)` and `getDocTool(deps)` live in `apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/kb-tools.ts`, with `deps = { search: KnowledgeSearchService; index: KnowledgeIndexService }`. Both tools resolve a `repo` (or a citation's `owner/name`) with `KnowledgeIndexService.resolveProjectRepo(ctx.projectId, { owner, name })`; null throws `NotFoundAppException`, so a deleted or foreign repository is `not_found`. A `path` that fails `isSafeFilterValue` is `ToolInputError('path')`. `koda-tool-descriptors.ts` gains `KODA_KB_SEARCH` and `KODA_GET_DOC`, appended to `KNOWLEDGE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS` (`:219`), which makes 12 of `KODA_TOOL_LIMITS.maxTools` 32. Both are `permission: { kind: 'member' }` and registered by `KnowledgeTools.onModuleInit` (`apps/api/src/fleet/assistant/tools/knowledge-tools.ts:241`), which gains `KnowledgeSearchService` and `KnowledgeIndexService`. - `koda_kb_search` input `{ query: string 1-500, repo?: "owner/name", pathPrefix?: string 1-300 with no `..` and no leading `/`, limit?: integer 1-20 (default 8) }`. Output: when `empty`, exactly `knowledge index is empty for this project`; when no hit, `no results`; otherwise a first line ` results for ""` (plus ` (lexical results only: embeddings unavailable)` when `lexicalOnly`), then per hit a line `[] /:@# — ` (`#` omitted when empty), a line `(status: [ → ])` when the chunk has a status, and `ctx.data(abstract + '\n' + snippet)`. An unknown `repo` throws `NotFoundAppException` (the executor answers `not_found`). - `koda_get_doc` input `{ citation: string }` or `{ repo: "owner/name", path: string, anchor?: string, part?: integer >= 1 }`. A citation matches `^([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)/([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+):([^@#]+)(?:@[0-9a-f]{7,40})?(?:#([a-z0-9_-]+))?$`; anything else is `ToolInputError('citation')`. A citation's sha is ignored: the answer is always the indexed text, labelled with the indexed sha. It reads the file's rows with `KnowledgeSearchService.readDoc(ctx.projectId, repo.id, path)`, drops chunk 0 (unless the file has no other chunk), keeps only rows whose `anchor` equals the requested anchor when one is given, and joins their `text` with a blank line. The text is split into parts of at most 12000 characters at line boundaries (a single line longer than 12000 characters is cut at 12000 characters, the rest starting the next part); the answer is a line `/:@ (indexed) part

of ` followed by `ctx.data(part text)`. A repository or file with no rows, an anchor with no rows, or a `part` beyond `m` throws `NotFoundAppException`. 1c-c-D14 (instructions): `KODA_TOOLS_LINE` (`apps/api/src/fleet/threads/thread-instructions.ts:7-8`) is appended with ` Search the project's docs with koda_kb_search and read them with koda_get_doc; cite docs as owner/name:path@sha7#anchor.` Both REPO and PROJECT instructions carry it. Use the existing executor's parse/member/execute pipeline, not a bypass. Validate malformed citations and unsafe paths in parse (where the executor maps ToolInputError to invalid_input); resolve missing repositories/files/anchors/parts in execution using NotFoundAppException. search calls carry ctx.projectId, default limit 8 and optional resolved repoId/pathPrefix; readDoc is the only indexed file read path. Do not access GitHub or honor a supplied citation sha as a historical fetch. Append descriptors in the exact order [KODA_MEMORY_SEARCH, KODA_TIMELINE, KODA_KB_SEARCH, KODA_GET_DOC]; keep input schemas aligned with parser validation and existing tool-count limits. AssistantModule imports KnowledgeModule. Existing `knowledge-tools.spec.ts` Test.createTestingModule provider list at :70-82 gains stub KnowledgeSearchService/KnowledgeIndexService values; its assertions are unchanged. Existing `thread-instructions.spec.ts` copy of KODA_TOOLS_LINE takes the appended text; placement assertions at :61-62, :98-99, :124-126 and :182-183 are unchanged. New tests must cover the AssistantToolExecutor.execute entry seam, membership context, exact output, data fencing and error mapping rather than testing only standalone string helpers. **Scope** — In: two tool factories/descriptors, KnowledgeTools registration/DI, member-only tool declarations and both thread instruction builders. Out: search ranking/readDoc implementation (US-002), indexer (US-004), queue/admin state routes (US-005), evaluation (US-007); no live/historical GitHub fetch, web link rendering, cross-project search or outcomes tools. **Interface** — `kbSearchTool(deps)` and `getDocTool(deps)`, with `deps = { search: KnowledgeSearchService; index: KnowledgeIndexService }`, implement `AssistantTool`; `permission: { kind: 'member' }`; koda_kb_search and koda_get_doc input/output grammars, citation regex and the instruction suffix are specified verbatim above.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] KNOWLEDGE_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS names koda_memory_search, koda_timeline, koda_kb_search and koda_get_doc in that order, and KODA_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS has at most KODA_TOOL_LIMITS.maxTools entries.
[unit] AssistantToolExecutor.execute of koda_kb_search { query: 'token cache' } for a job of project p1 calls KnowledgeSearchService.search with { projectId: 'p1', query: 'token cache', limit: 8 }.

[unit] With one hit { owner: 'o', name: 'n', path: 'docs/a.md', sha: 'abcdef1234', anchor: 'cache', headingPath: 'A > Cache' }, the result's first line is 1 results for "token cache" and the second is [1] o/n:docs/a.md@abcdef1#cache — A > Cache.
[unit] The hit's abstract and snippet appear inside the call's koda-data fence (passed through ctx.data).
[unit] A hit with status: 'superseded' and supersededBy: 'docs/adr/0009.md' adds the line (status: superseded → docs/adr/0009.md).

[unit] With lexicalOnly: true, the first line ends with (lexical results only: embeddings unavailable); with empty: true the whole result is knowledge index is empty for this project; with no hits it is no results.

[unit] koda_kb_search with query: '', with a 501-character query, with limit: 21 and with pathPrefix: '../x' each answers invalid_input with reasons query, query, limit and pathPrefix (one table-driven test).

[unit] koda_kb_search with repo: 'o/missing', and koda_get_doc with { repo: 'o/missing', path: 'docs/a.md' }, each answer not_found when KnowledgeIndexService.resolveProjectRepo resolves null (one table-driven test).

[unit] koda_get_doc with { citation: 'o/n:docs/a.md@1111111#cache' }, over rows indexed at sha abcdef1234, calls KnowledgeSearchService.readDoc(projectId, <id of o/n>, 'docs/a.md') and answers a first line o/n:docs/a.md@abcdef1 (indexed) part 1 of 1 followed by the fenced text of the rows whose anchor is cache.

[unit] Given docs/a.md has section chunks in addition to summary chunk 0, koda_get_doc with { repo: 'o/n', path: 'docs/a.md' } answers the text of every chunk except chunk 0, joined by a blank line, in chunkIndex order.
[unit] A document held in one row whose text is 30 lines of 999 characters joined by \n (29999 characters) answers part 1 of 3 for part absent, part 3 of 3 for part: 3, and not_found for part: 4.

[unit] koda_get_doc with { citation: 'not a citation' } answers invalid_input: citation, with { repo: 'o/n', path: "docs/it's.md" } answers invalid_input: path, and with an anchor no row carries answers not_found.
[unit] A document that is one 13000-character line answers part 1 of 2 whose text is its first 12000 characters.

[unit] buildProjectThreadInstructions and buildThreadInstructions both return text whose koda tools: line ends with cite docs as owner/name:path@sha7#anchor. and names koda_kb_search and koda_get_doc, preserving the existing memory:<id> guidance and placement immediately before the skills block for both empty and non-empty skill snapshots.

userStories.title: Evaluation script
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a deterministic scoring function and authenticated REST evaluation CLI over the reviewed 40-question repository-doc fixture.

**Motivation** — The 2026-10-15 knowledge research found that koda's gap is content and reach, not retrieval sophistication: the project's architecture, specs, design documents and ADRs live as repository Markdown that no thread can reach.

**Approach** — 1c-c-D15 (evaluation): `apps/api/test/kb-eval/questions.json` (committed with this spec, not written by a story) is an array of 40 `{ id: string, question: string, expected: Array<{ repo: string; path: string; anchor?: string }> }`. `apps/api/scripts/kb-eval.ts` exports pure `scoreRun(questions, answers): KbEvalReport`, where `answers` maps a question id to its ranked hits and `KbEvalReport` is `{ questions: number; recallAt5: number; recallAt20: number; mrr: number; anchorRecallAt20: number; misses: string[] }`. A question counts toward recall@k when any of its `expected` `{repo, path}` appears among its first k hits; `mrr` averages `1 / rank` of the first matching hit (0 when none); `anchorRecallAt20` also requires the anchor when the expected entry has one; `misses` lists the ids with no match in the first 20. No reranker, no Jina provider, no code embeddings, no LLM-written abstracts or context lines (S5b-R14).
Only the default branch is indexed; other branches, tags and pull request heads are not.
Chunks of a deleted fleet repository are not removed from LanceDB; search drops them (1c-c-D7).
No GitHub `push` webhook; freshness comes from the poll, the merge hook and the admin route.
No search across projects; every query is scoped to one project's table.
No per-repository chunk cap; the 2000-file and 256 KB-per-file caps bound a pass.

Setext headings (a line underlined with `===` or `---`) are not section headings, and anchors drop non-ASCII characters where GitHub keeps them, so a non-ASCII heading's anchor can differ from GitHub's.
The `evaluate:retrieval` script and its synthetic documents are unchanged.
Passing `KNOWLEDGE_INDEX_ENABLED` and `KNOWLEDGE_POLL_MS` through the koda-wk compose file, and registering `nathapp-io/koda` as a fleet repository, are deployment steps, not story work.
`apps/api/test/kb-eval/questions.json` is authored with this spec and reviewed by the user; no story writes or edits it.
US-004 only: two API instances do not coordinate passes beyond the database lease; koda runs one API instance.
US-005 only: the in-process queue does not survive an API restart; the next poll re-queues every repository.
